paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes a training-free inference-time cache reuse method for interleaved multimodal reasoning, addressing positional mismatch in historical visual KV cache reuse.
dominant_domain: Interleaved multimodal reasoning, visual revisiting, KV cache reuse, RoPE position rebinding, efficient MLLM inference.
must_cover: Direct historical visual KV cache reuse fails because cached keys are bound to their original RoPE positions.
The failure can cause attention perturbation, decoding collapse, and repeated-token loops.
PRCR stores pre-RoPE raw visual K/V projections and original spatial coordinates during multimodal prefill.
At a later reasoning step, selected visual entries are reassigned to positions compatible with the current decoding context.
Reconstructed visual cache is concatenated with the active decoder cache, enabling replay-free visual revisiting.
PRCR matches or slightly exceeds token replay accuracy while reducing visual-revisiting FLOPs by orders of magnitude.
key_numbers: On M3CoT with Qwen3-VL-8B, direct KV reuse drops overall accuracy from 66.44 to 23.50 and has an 81.04 stuck rate.
Qwen3-VL-8B M3CoT ALL: baseline 66.44, Token-Replay 68.46, PRCR 68.68.
Reinsertion ablation on M3CoT: Direct KV Reuse 23.50 accuracy and 81.04 stuck rate; LPA 63.03 and 7.93; UIR 67.45 and 0; PCR 68.68 and 0.
Best left extension length is L=2 on M3CoT and MathVista.
Qwen3-VL-32B with K=128: Token-Replay 7.75T FLOPs versus PRCR 125.83M FLOPs, with 192MB extra memory.
real_comparisons: Compared with baseline MCoT, PRCR enables interleaved visual revisiting without repeatedly forwarding selected visual tokens.
Compared with Token-Replay, PRCR reconstructs visual KV cache from raw prefill memory and avoids replaying visual evidence.
Compared with Direct KV Reuse, PRCR rebinds positions before cache insertion and prevents collapse.
Compared with visual-token reinjection methods such as VisRef, PRCR focuses on cache-level systems efficiency rather than token selection quality.

central_claims.claim: Direct historical visual KV cache reuse fails because cached visual keys carry stale positional bindings.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The paper shows large accuracy collapse, high stuck rate, and attention perturbation under direct reuse, and links the failure to RoPE position mismatch.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that every cache reuse failure in every positional encoding scheme has the same cause.

central_claims.claim: Position rebinding can make cached visual evidence reusable without token replay.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: PRCR with PCR matches or slightly exceeds Token-Replay on the tested benchmarks while avoiding repeated visual forwarding.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not show benefits when the revisited visual evidence requires new local crops, zooms, or dynamic-resolution re-encoding.

central_claims.claim: PCR is the best of the tested position reassignment strategies.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Table 2 shows PCR has the highest M3CoT accuracy and zero stuck rate among Direct Reuse, LPA, UIR, and PCR.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not exhaust all possible learned or model-specific cache reinsertion layouts.

claim_boundaries: The method assumes access to pre-RoPE raw layer-wise visual K/V projections during multimodal prefill.
PRCR is training-free but implementation-dependent; it needs modification of the inference cache path.
The current method reuses visual entries that already exist in prefill; it does not support new zoomed or re-encoded evidence without extra work.
Reported gains are on M3CoT, MathVista, MMStar, and MMMU with Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 backbones.
negative_or_limiting_results: Direct KV Reuse has 23.50 accuracy and 81.04 stuck rate on M3CoT, demonstrating severe failure.
LPA still has a non-zero stuck rate of 7.93, so simply inserting cache around the current position is insufficient.
The authors state that PRCR loses its computational advantage when visual revisiting requires new local zoom, scaling, or dynamic-resolution encoding.
PRCR adds raw visual evidence memory, although the reported overhead is small in percentage terms.
mechanism_result_map: Stale RoPE positions map to Figure 3 attention perturbation and Figure 2 decoding collapse.
Raw Visual Evidence Memory maps to the ability to reconstruct visual keys at new positions.
PCR position reassignment maps to Table 2, where PCR achieves the best accuracy and zero stuck rate.
Replay-free cache decoding maps to Table 3, where PRCR reduces visual-revisiting FLOPs from trillions or hundreds of billions to millions.
comparative_positioning: PRCR complements ICoT and DaP-ICoT by making repeated visual revisiting cheaper at the cache level.
PRCR complements SDR-MCoT because SDR-MCoT controls whether to reason and where to attend, while PRCR controls how to revisit visual evidence efficiently.
PRCR complements VisRef because VisRef selects visual token coresets, while PRCR handles replay-free reinsertion of visual evidence.
In the TrainingFree collection, PRCR is the most systems-oriented paper.
reuse_takeaways: For 3D agent systems, cache reuse must preserve coordinate and position consistency; simply reusing old memory can corrupt later reasoning.
Store raw evidence before positional binding if future revisiting is expected.
Separate evidence selection from evidence reinsertion; PRCR assumes a selected set and solves the reinsertion problem.
When evaluating visual revisiting, report stuck loops or decoding collapse, not only accuracy.
followup_questions: Can PRCR be combined with a visual coreset selector such as VisRef to choose the entries to rebind?
Can raw visual evidence memory be made multi-scale so local zoom evidence can also be reused?
Would learned position reassignment outperform PCR while preserving zero stuck rate?
How does PRCR behave with non-RoPE positional encodings or with architectures that encode visual positions differently?
